# Matthew Cuthbert

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c1 P4](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v1 c37 P9](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0009), [v1 c37 P11](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0011)</sub>

## Appearance

Matthew Cuthbert was known to dress up in a white collar when driving in a buggy on rare outings. Upon his death, he lay in his coffin framed by long gray hair with a placid face and a kindly smile.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P4](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0004), [v1 c37 P11](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0011)_

## Personality

Matthew was an extraordinarily shy, quiet, and taciturn man who rarely left home and hated talking to strangers or being in public. Despite his quiet nature, he was deeply soft-hearted, kind, and sympathetic, particularly towards Anne, taking her part and feeling delighted by her speech. Some people considered him odd or even crazy because of his peculiar mannerisms and infatuation with Anne's talking.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P2](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0002), [v1 c1 P4](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0004), [v1 c4 P26](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0026), [v1 c10 P1](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0001), [v1 c10 P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002), [v1 c13 P0](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0000), [v1 c25 P13](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0013), [v1 c37 P10](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0010), [v2 c15 P0](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0000)_

## History

Matthew lived at Green Gables with his sister Marilla, keeping mostly to himself and avoiding public life. In early June, he dressed up and went to Carmody to fetch Anne Shirley, whom he brought home to Green Gables despite his usual fear of strangers. He quickly grew fond of Anne, enjoying her chatter, taking her side during disagreements, and offering her quiet support. He lived a quiet life tilling the fields and tending the homestead until his sudden death caused by the shock of reading about the failure of the Abbey Bank. He passed away instantaneously with a peaceful expression and was buried in Avonlea, where Anne maintained a weekly pilgrimage to his grave long after his passing.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P2](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0002), [v1 c1 P4](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0004), [v1 c2 P14](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0014), [v1 c2 P16](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0016), [v1 c10 P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002), [v1 c13 P0](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0000), [v1 c37 P9](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0009), [v1 c37 P10](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0010), [v1 c37 P11](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0011), [v1 c37 P21](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0021), [v2 c15 P0](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0000)_
